channel.title: Omniverse Compute (OMC) — News & Announcements
channel.description: Official Omniverse Compute (OMC) updates: testnet milestones, airdrop campaigns, engineering progress and governance announcements.

item.title: DCF forum: the workers-per-megawatt bottleneck — why a GW-scale AI site needs a small army, not just silicon
item.description: New on forum.omc.network: a deep dive on the labor queue behind AI compute. A single gigawatt of data-center capacity draws a large skilled-trades workforce — electricians, pipefitters, and cooling specialists — while lead times for transformers and switchgear now rival the GPU wait. Read the deep dive →

item.title: DCF forum: the network-fabric tax — why 800G ports and radix math cap cluster scale
item.description: New on forum.omc.network: a deep dive on the interconnect, the compute bill everyone prices last. 800G ports, the radix math behind spine-leaf topology, and why one oversubscribed uplink can stall an entire training run. Read the deep dive →

item.title: The OMC airdrop is open: 20,000,000 OMC, 1,000,000 slots, free to join
item.description: Registration is live. 20,000,000 OMC is split into 1,000,000 slots of 20 OMC each, first come first served. No purchase and no presale — three social tasks plus a wallet signature. Claiming opens 1 January 2027 with a 0.01 BNB processing fee per entry. Read the announcement →

item.title: AITop glossary: quantization — the bits-per-weight dial that decides if a 70B model fits your GPU
item.description: New on top.omc.network: a plain-English glossary entry on quantization, the one formula (VRAM ≈ params × bytes/weight) every local-LLM buyer needs, and why Q4_K_M is the default. Read the glossary →

item.title: DCF forum: the 12x water multiplier — 92% of a data center's water footprint sits at the power plant
item.description: New on forum.omc.network: a deep dive showing US data centers used 66B liters on site in 2023 vs ~800B generating their power — a 12x multiplier that rewrites the closed-loop cooling debate. Read the full breakdown →

item.title: Contracts redeployed: the slashing and fee burns now reduce supply
item.description: Our own review found that the two “burn” paths only moved tokens to a dead address, so totalSupply() never fell — a weak mechanism doing a different job from the one we had documented. Slashing and the settlement fee now call burn() on the token, and the whole set was redeployed in a cascade (the market stores the staking address, so both moved together). Verified on-chain: one 6.0 tOMC slash cut total supply by exactly 1.2, its 20% burn share. New addresses are in the site footer and on the Testnet page.

item.title: Self-review published — with reproducible bytecode verification
item.description: The full security self-review is public: one High-severity defect (the refund path could not execute at all) was found and fixed, and the fix is deployed. Bytecode verification confirms the contracts running on testnet match the reviewed source, and property-based tests run 2,762 assertions against a real EVM. Being precise about what this is: automated testing plus a manual read-through by the team, not a third-party audit.

item.title: Ecosystem grows to three sites: DCF forum and AITop are live
item.description: The OMC ecosystem now spans omc.network, top.omc.network (independent, no-affiliate AI tool rankings) and forum.omc.network — the Decentralized Compute Forum, with in-depth essays and open comment sections. All three are cross-linked.

item.title: Industry voice: Jensen Huang — data centers are becoming “AI factories”
item.description: At GTC 2024, NVIDIA's CEO described a shift from file-cabinet data centers to AI factories that manufacture a new commodity at scale: intelligence. Compute and power — not chips — are becoming the binding constraint. Industry commentary, not an endorsement of OMC. Related analysis →

item.title: Industry voice: Vitalik Buterin — decentralized computing belongs in the d/acc toolbox
item.description: In his November 2024 essay “d/acc”, the Ethereum founder argues that open, verifiable and decentralized computing is a defensive technology worth building — including markets that route idle GPUs to real workloads. Industry commentary, not an endorsement of OMC. Related analysis →

item.title: DCF forum launches the GPU pricing deep-dive series
item.description: New on forum.omc.network: a Pricing Watch series covering the real cost of a training run, H100 rate spreads between hyperscalers and decentralized marketplaces, and the reserved-vs-spot arbitrage. No sponsors, no affiliate links — the methodology is published with every piece.

item.title: Industry voice: Sam Altman — the cost of intelligence trends toward the cost of energy
item.description: In “The Intelligence Age” (September 2024), OpenAI's CEO argues that intelligence becomes a utility as its cost falls toward the price of energy — making compute supply and power access the hard constraints. Industry commentary, not an endorsement of OMC. Related analysis →

item.title: Roadmap updated: mainnet set for 1 January 2027
item.description: Phase 1 covers testnet contract deployment on BNB Chain, the open-source node client, the public testnet and the 2% community airdrop. Participation is open now; mainnet — together with the airdrop claim window and staking — opens on 1 January 2027, so the OMC a wallet accumulates during the campaign becomes claimable and stakeable at the same moment. Zero-knowledge verification research and full DAO governance follow from 2027 Q4.

item.title: Phase 1 testnet is live on BNB Chain
item.description: The OMC public testnet is deployed to BNB Smart Chain Testnet (Chain ID 97). The test contract is verified on BscScan, and the RPC endpoints, faucet guidance and the four-step node onboarding guide are published on the Testnet page.

item.title: Community airdrop: participation open, claim at mainnet · 1 January 2027
item.description: 20,000,000 OMC — 2% of the fixed supply — is reserved for the community: 1,000,000 entries × 20 OMC. Up to 5 entries per wallet and 1 per day (resets 00:00 UTC+8). Registration is open now: complete the three social tasks and register entries ahead of launch. A base claim is 100 OMC and a maxed-out wallet holds 200 OMC; claiming costs a non-refundable 0.01 BNB, which funds development. Claiming opens with mainnet and staking on 1 January 2027, so the OMC a wallet accumulates can be staked the day it exists.

item.title: Whitepaper v2.0 published
item.description: The full technical reference is live: the three-tier architecture, verification and slashing rules, the weighted task-matching engine and the complete tokenomics with vesting schedules — as a web page and as PDF downloads.

item.title: Project repository open-sourced
item.description: The repository is public: website source, whitepaper documents, contribution guide and an MIT license. Node operators and contributors can follow the client roadmap and open issues directly.

item.title: Anti-scam notice: registering is free, claiming costs 0.01 BNB
item.description: We never ask for your seed phrase, private key, or to send BNB to a wallet address. The only payment is the 0.01 BNB claim fee charged inside the claim transaction itself — any contract named OMC outside official announcements is fraudulent.
